name: Jake Holloway
summary: A 22-year-old graduate living in a shared house in Manchester, comfortable with technology and keen to manage finances smartly while navigating adult responsibilities for the first time. As a junior developer, he expects seamless digital experiences and avoids phone calls.
quote: I've done all the research and found us a better deal, but getting everyone to actually sit down and agree is like herding cats. And I really don't want to be the one chasing people for money every month.

demographics.background: Jake graduated last year and moved into a shared house with three friends from university. This is his first experience managing household bills and he's determined to be savvy about it. He works as a junior developer and is careful with money while still enjoying socialising and gaming.

needs.need: Feel in control of his finances and adult responsibilities
Be seen as reliable and capable by his housemates
Avoid unexpected costs or nasty surprises
Learn how things work so he can handle them confidently in future

frustrations.frustration: Feels overwhelmed by 'adulting' tasks he was never taught how to handle
Dislikes phone calls and prefers to sort things out digitally
Gets frustrated when processes seem unnecessarily complicated

motivations.motivation: Wants to prove he can handle adult responsibilities independently
Motivated by getting a good deal and saving money
Values fairness and doing right by his housemates

technology.description: As a developer, Jake is highly comfortable with technology. He uses apps for everything from banking to fitness tracking and expects seamless digital experiences.

communication.style: Direct and efficient - appreciates clear, jargon-free communication that gets to the point

influences.description: Trusts recommendations from friends and fellow young professionals over advertising
Checks Reddit, Trustpilot, and comparison sites before making decisions
Follows accounts like MoneySavingExpert on social media

decisionMaking.style: Analytical but efficient - wants enough information to feel confident but won't over-research

behaviouralPatterns.context: Will spend time comparing options online before committing, but once decided, wants to complete quickly
If a process becomes too complicated, may abandon it or postpone indefinitely

contexts.title: Energy Provider Switcher (Shared House)
contexts.description: A consumer responsible for finding, selecting, and setting up a new energy provider for a shared rental property, coordinating with multiple housemates on decisions and bill-splitting.

needs.need: Find a competitively priced energy deal that works for everyone in the house
Understand how the switching process works and what steps are required
Set up fair and straightforward bill-splitting arrangements with housemates
Ensure a smooth transition with no gap in supply
Avoid being personally liable if housemates don't pay their share
Keep housemates informed and get their agreement on the chosen provider

frustrations.frustration: Coordinating decisions with multiple people who have different priorities and availability
Uncertainty about who is responsible for the account in a shared tenancy
Difficulty finding clear information about how switching works for renters
Confusing tariff structures and hidden fees that make comparison difficult
Chase effort required to collect bill money from housemates each month
Lack of transparency about estimated usage for a shared property

channels.usageContext: Primary channel for account management, meter readings, and usage tracking
Queries and problem resolution without phone calls
Last resort for issues that cannot be resolved digitally

details.shoppingBehaviour: Comparison-focused, uses price comparison sites and seeks peer recommendations
details.purchasingContext: First-time energy account holder, making decision on behalf of household
details.brandRelationships: No established loyalty to energy brands; open to newer providers if well-reviewed
decisionFactors: No exit fees (flexibility for tenancy changes)
Positive reviews from other young renters
details.budgetConstraints: Cost-conscious; needs to balance affordable rates with housemate buy-in
details.currentProviderSituation: Inherited from previous tenants, on standard variable rate

momentsThatMatter.moment: Getting housemates to agree on a provider
Collecting first month's contributions from housemates
Encountering a problem requiring phone contact

goalsAsExperienced.goal: Find a good energy deal quickly using comparison tools, then get housemates aligned so he can complete the switch
Set up a bill-splitting system that runs itself without awkward monthly conversations
Complete the entire switching process digitally without needing to make phone calls
Prove to himself and his housemates that he can handle this adult responsibility competently
Protect himself from being left out of pocket if housemates don't pay

painPoints.painPoint: His efficient research-then-act style collides with the need to get consensus from three other people with varying levels of interest and availability
painPoints.emergesFrom: Jake's preference for quick, decisive action meets the role's requirement to coordinate group decisions

painPoints.painPoint: The social awkwardness of chasing housemates for money conflicts with his desire to maintain good relationships and be seen as capable, not naggy
painPoints.emergesFrom: Jake's need for recognition and belonging clashes with the ongoing administrative burden of being account holder

painPoints.painPoint: His phone-avoidance creates friction when energy providers require calls for account setup, meter readings, or problem resolution
painPoints.emergesFrom: Jake's strong communication preferences meet an industry that still relies heavily on phone-based customer service

painPoints.painPoint: Anxiety about being personally liable for the full bill undermines his sense of security and control
painPoints.emergesFrom: Jake's need for security conflicts with the legal reality that one person must be the named account holder

painPoints.painPoint: His expectation of intuitive digital experiences is frustrated by comparison sites and provider websites that feel dated or overly complex
painPoints.emergesFrom: As a developer used to well-designed apps, Jake finds the energy sector's digital experience disappointing

opportunities: Provide a clear, step-by-step switching guide specifically for renters and shared houses
Offer built-in bill-splitting functionality with automated payment collection from housemates
Enable fully digital account management including webchat for all support queries
Create shareable comparison summaries Jake can send to housemates for quick approval
Provide transparent, simple tariffs that are easy to compare without hidden complexity
Offer flexible contracts with no exit fees to match typical tenancy lengths
Send proactive notifications and reminders that reduce the admin burden on the account holder
emergence.emotionalContext: Jake approaches this task with a mix of determination and mild anxiety. He wants to prove he can handle adult responsibilities and is motivated by getting a good deal, but he's nervous about the social dynamics of money and the unfamiliar territory of energy contracts.

useCases.trigger: Rate increase notification from current provider
useCases.outcome: Clear understanding of costs, easy to share findings with housemates
Complete process in one session digitally
Quick submission via app in under a minute
Issue resolved via webchat without phone call

successMetrics: At least 10% reduction in monthly costs vs previous tariff
Switch completed in under 3 weeks from housemate agreement
Zero phone calls required throughout the process
All housemates pay within 3 days of bill
No complaints from housemates about the choice or process

relationships.description: Jake is the primary actor in the energy supplier switch mission

aiToolsUsed.usage: Conversion from v1.1 persona, role, and pairing artifacts to v2.0 Actor format

governance.retentionPolicy: Retain for project duration + 12 months, then review
governance.legalBasis: Legitimate interest — service design and user experience improvement
